features.name: share_comments_statistical_terms
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments contain statistical language such as percentages or averages?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. If missing or malformed, return null. If the list is empty, return null. A comment counts if re.search(r'\d\s*(%|percent\b|per cent\b)|\b(percent|percentage|average|averages|averaged|mean|median|statistic|statistics|statistical)\b', comment, re.I) matches (case-insensitive literal/regex match, no semantic filtering). Return count of matching comments divided by total number of comments.

h0: share_comments_statistical_terms has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: A higher share_comments_statistical_terms is associated with a higher probability of delta.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (association only, not causal). Statistical language is operationalized as a mechanical regex for percentages and average-type words (percent, average, mean, median, statistic*); this is a lexical proxy, and "mean" may match non-statistical uses. Comments are unordered with no per-comment outcomes, so the share is row-level only. Raw comment text may contain delta/view-change announcements or other outcome contamination, and timing relative to the outcome is unknown. Empty comment list gives null (share).
